intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that common variable immunodeficiency-15 (CVID15) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SEC61A1 gene on chromosome 3.

paragraphs.text: Common variable immunodeficiency-15 (CVID15) is a primary antibody deficiency. It is characterized by hypogammaglobulinemia affecting IgM, IgG, and IgA, and by severe recurrent bacterial infections of the respiratory tract that usually begin in the first year of life. Peripheral B- and T-cell subpopulations are normal, but B cells have an intrinsic defect in differentiating into plasma cells. Expressivity is variable: within affected families the phenotype has ranged from transient hypogammaglobulinemia and specific antibody deficiency to CVID (Schubert et al., 2018).

paragraphs.text: Schubert et al. (2018) studied 10 individuals from a family (family I) who had antibody isotype deficiencies involving IgM, IgG, and IgA. They had severe recurrent bacterial infections, including tonsillitis, otitis, sinusitis, pneumonia, and gastrointestinal infections. Disease onset was mostly in the first year of life. Affected individuals did not respond to polysaccharide vaccination, and their responses to tetanus toxin vaccination varied. Since starting intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) replacement therapy, they had had a marked decrease in the number and severity of infections. B, T, and NK cells were present in normal ratios, and detailed T-cell phenotyping was normal, including numbers of regulatory T cells and recent thymic emigrants. Peripheral B-cell subpopulations were also normal, including naive, unswitched memory, switched memory, IgA+, IgG+, transitional, and CD21-low B cells. Only the very small population of peripheral CD27+CD38-high plasmablasts appeared reduced in family I, although the authors considered this value error-prone. Patients had no clinical symptoms other than infections. Serum levels of proteins secreted by the liver and pancreas were normal, as were laboratory values that are altered in autosomal dominant tubulointerstitial kidney disease.

paragraphs.text: In a second, unrelated family (family II), Schubert et al. (2018) described an 8-year-old boy who had had hypogammaglobulinemia since birth. Because he was treated with IVIG, he had not had severe or recurrent infections. Repeated attempts to withdraw IVIG failed because his serum Ig levels stayed low. His grandmother, who also carried the mutation, reported more frequent upper respiratory infections in childhood, with recurrent bilateral bacterial otitis media. At age 66 years she had normal serum immunoglobulin levels. The boy's mother also carried the mutation but was not included in the study because she had a secondary immunodeficiency.

paragraphs.text: Schubert et al. (2018) performed whole-exome sequencing on 4 affected and 2 unaffected members of family I, which had autosomal dominant primary antibody deficiency. Among the shared variants, only one fell within the linkage region on chromosome 3: a heterozygous c.254T-A transversion in the SEC61A1 gene, resulting in a val85-to-asp (V85D) substitution. Sanger sequencing showed that the mutation segregated perfectly with the disease in the family. V85 is a highly conserved residue and one of 6 bulky hydrophobic amino acids that form the pore ring of the Sec61 channel. In HeLa cells in which endogenous SEC61A1 was silenced and then replaced, the V85D mutant channel showed significantly reduced cotranslational translocation of preprolactin compared with wildtype. Overexpressing the mutant in HeLa cells reduced the ER calcium load, consistent with increased calcium leakage, and the authors concluded this was a dominant effect. Stable expression of the V85D mutant caused transduced cells of 3 multiple myeloma cell lines to disappear and induced the terminal unfolded protein response, including upregulation of ATF4 and CHOP. Other lymphoid and nonlymphoid cell lines were not affected. In thapsigargin-sensitized HEK293T cells, the mutant also had a dominant effect on XBP1s induction when coexpressed with wildtype SEC61A1.

paragraphs.text: Schubert et al. (2018) also performed targeted next-generation sequencing in more than 200 additional patients with primary antibody deficiency. They identified a heterozygous c.1325G-T transversion in the SEC61A1 gene, resulting in a glu381-to-ter (E381X) substitution, in the 8-year-old boy from family II. Sanger sequencing confirmed the mutation and found it in 2 more family members, his mother and grandmother. The gnomAD database contained no premature stop variants in SEC61A1. In naive B cells from the boy and his grandmother, SEC61A1 protein levels were reduced, whereas levels in T cells were comparable to control. No truncated protein was detected in an EBV-transformed B-cell line from the boy. The authors concluded that the mutation likely causes nonsense-mediated mRNA decay and SEC61A1 haploinsufficiency.

paragraphs.text: Schubert et al. (2018) noted that SEC61A1 is a target gene of spliced XBP1 and is strongly induced during plasma cell differentiation. By proteomics, SEC61A protein was 2-fold more abundant in human plasmablasts than in naive and memory B cells. They proposed that plasma cells may need 2 functional SEC61A1 alleles to make enough SEC61A1 protein for high-level immunoglobulin production. They suggested that SEC61A1 haploinsufficiency causes hypogammaglobulinemia with variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance in family II. In family I, they proposed that the dominant-negative V85D mutation causes a functional haploinsufficiency combined with disturbed calcium homeostasis, resulting in fully penetrant disease.

paragraphs.text: Schubert et al. (2018) studied a family (family I) with primary antibody deficiency affecting IgM, IgG, and IgA and with severe recurrent bacterial infections. paragraphs.text: Schubert et al. (2018) studied an 8-year-old boy (family II) who had had hypogammaglobulinemia since birth. By targeted sequencing they identified a heterozygous c.1325G-T transversion in the SEC61A1 gene, resulting in a glu381-to-ter (E381X) substitution. The mutation was also present in his mother and in his grandmother, who had had recurrent otitis media in childhood but had normal immunoglobulin levels at age 66. In the boy and his grandmother, SEC61A1 protein was reduced in naive B cells. No truncated protein was detected, consistent with nonsense-mediated decay and haploinsufficiency. The boy's B cells showed reduced differentiation into plasma cells in vitro.

checks.claim: The 8-year-old boy from family II studied by Schubert et al. (2018) had had hypogammaglobulinemia since birth.
checks.evidence_quote: was an eight year old boy who had hypogammaglobulinemia since birth

checks.claim: Targeted sequencing identified a heterozygous c.1325G-T transversion in the SEC61A1 gene, resulting in a glu381-to-ter (E381X) substitution, in the boy from family II.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified a heterozygous nonsense mutation (c.1325G>T, p.E381*) in individual II.P3 from Family II
checks.explanation: The mutation was found by targeted NGS.

checks.claim: The SEC61A1 E381X mutation was also present in the boy's mother and grandmother.
checks.evidence_quote: His mother (who is affected by a secondary immunodeficiency and therefore not included in this study) and grandmother (II.P1) are also mutation carriers

checks.claim: The grandmother in family II had recurrent otitis media in childhood.
checks.evidence_quote: reported an increased frequency of upper respiratory infections during childhood with recurrent bilateral bacterial otitis media

checks.claim: The grandmother in family II had normal immunoglobulin levels at age 66.
checks.evidence_quote: Now, at age 66, she has normal immunoglobulin serum levels

checks.claim: SEC61A1 protein was reduced in naive B cells from the boy and his grandmother in family II.
checks.evidence_quote: We observed reduced expression levels of SEC61A1 in naïve B cells of II.P1 and II.P3

checks.claim: No truncated SEC61A1 E381X protein was detected, consistent with nonsense-mediated decay and haploinsufficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: we excluded the presence of a shortened protein product from the mutated allele in Family II (Figure S1), supporting the hypothesis that the nonsense mutation p.E381* likely results in nonsense-mediated mRNA decay and leads to SEC61A1 haploinsufficiency

checks.claim: B cells from the boy in family II showed reduced differentiation into plasma cells in vitro.
checks.evidence_quote: was significantly decreased in mutation carriers from both families upon T cell dependent (Figure 3A, B) and T cell independent (Figure S2A, B) stimulation
checks.explanation: The paper reports reduced differentiation for carriers from Family II as a group but does not single out the boy's B cells in the text.
